title: Modbus Write Single Coil Detection for Monitored Conpot Endpoint

approval.blocking_condition: Confirm the required packet fields in the canonical OT PCAP and resolve all blocking evidence findings.

purpose: Define the exact OT network behavior that a later candidate detection must identify, without treating a coil write alone as proof of malicious intent.

scope.in_scope_activity: Modbus Write Single Coil request using function code 5
out_of_scope_activity: Modbus Write Multiple Coils using function code 15
Modbus function-code-5 responses from the monitored endpoint
claims of malicious intent based only on a write

detection_behavior.plain_language: Generate one alert for each Modbus function-code-5 request sent from any source to 10.10.20.10 on TCP port 502.
prohibited_match_restrictions: source IP 10.10.10.30 or any other fixed source
prohibited_behavior: match function-code-5 requests to destinations other than 10.10.20.10:502
detection_behavior.rationale: The observed baseline contains reads only, so a single-coil control write is the relevant behavior. Leaving the source, coil address, value, and unit ID unrestricted avoids overfitting the detection to one rehearsed transaction.

pcap_confirmation_required: controlled action is a request toward 10.10.20.10
wire-level coil address is recorded as context
encoded coil value is recorded as context
source IP is 10.10.10.30 for the demonstrated controlled action
restoration is also a function-code-5 request
capture interface and location are recorded
whether the capture observes both request and response is recorded
evidence_requirements.evidence_boundary: Script JSON describes intended and reported behavior; the canonical PCAP provides packet-level proof. Address, value, and unit ID must be extracted from the PCAP or correlated Modbus transaction evidence rather than assumed to appear in an alert.

correlation.method: Correlate the PCAP, write JSON, restore JSON, and alert evidence using transaction identifiers where available and timestamps within the documented tolerance.

test_matrix.traffic: Function-code-5 request to a destination other than 10.10.20.10:502
Function-code-5 request from a source other than 10.10.10.30 to 10.10.20.10:502
Function code 15 or a Modbus register-write request to 10.10.20.10:502

test_matrix.expected_result: Record parser outcome; it must not count as a successful function-code-5 detection.

validation_requirements.pass_condition: The controlled action and restoration request each have exactly one corresponding unique alert; every alert produced by the candidate detection is explained; baseline reads do not alert; required negative and generalization tests produce their specified outcomes; and semantic inspection confirms that no prohibited restriction or behavior was introduced.
validation_requirements.reporting_boundary: Report observed matches and test outcomes. Do not claim a false-positive rate, detection accuracy, or general OT coverage from this limited dataset.

reject_if_candidate: uses an action other than alert

implementation_prerequisites.purpose: Record later environment facts required before a candidate detection can be tested; these fields do not define the AI generation or deployment workflow.
implementation_prerequisites.requirement: Test any candidate using the same Suricata version and relevant configuration intended for the lab sensor.

known_limitations: The detection identifies a control write, not attacker intent.
A legitimate maintenance write using function code 5 will also match.
The controlled action and restoration are intentionally indistinguishable to this network detection.
The reads-only baseline is too small to establish accuracy or a false-positive rate.
The specification covers one monitored Conpot endpoint and does not claim general OT coverage.
untested_assumptions: The canonical controlled action and restoration use Modbus function code 5.
The selected capture point observes the required request traffic.
The intended Suricata environment can parse Modbus traffic with its deployed configuration.
Missing conformance cases can be represented safely with clearly labeled synthetic PCAPs.

blocking_findings: Canonical PCAP fields and capture visibility have not yet been confirmed.
Evidence hashes and time-correlation parameters have not yet been recorded.
Suricata environment and Modbus parser status have not yet been recorded.
resolved_findings: Defined one exact request behavior and prohibited source, address, value, unit-ID, and payload overfitting.
Replaced minimum alert counts with transaction-level attribution and explained-alert requirements.
Added negative and alternate-source conformance tests.
Separated detection requirements from response, deployment, and AI-generation policy.
Defined restoration as an expected matching write that requires external context for attribution.
Separated known limitations from untested assumptions.
Normalized lifecycle status and preserved v1 as the superseded specification.
blackbox_review.approval_gate: Populate and verify all required evidence and environment fields, execute the conformance matrix, rerun black-box review, resolve all blocking findings, and obtain explicit evidence approval before changing lifecycle_status to APPROVED_FOR_GENERATION.
